sections.overview: The Common Firecrest is a tiny Eurasian songbird in the kinglet family, found chiefly in Europe and north-western Africa.
sections.identification: Its bold black-and-white facial stripes and crest distinguish it from the Goldcrest; the male crest is orange, while the female’s is yellow.
sections.habitat: It uses coniferous woodland and also some mixed or evergreen broadleaf woods.
sections.diet: It feeds on small insects and other invertebrates, gleaned among foliage and sometimes caught while hovering.
sections.behavior: In autumn and winter it may join mixed foraging flocks with tits and other small woodland birds.
sections.reproduction: The female builds the nest and incubates; both parents feed the young.
sections.ecology: Where it overlaps the Goldcrest, the Firecrest tends to take larger prey and forage on different leaf and branch surfaces, which can reduce direct competition.
sections.conservation: It is assessed as Least Concern globally.
